purpose: This eye drop is used to treat bacterial eye infections, most commonly bacterial conjunctivitis, which is sometimes called 'pink eye.' It helps clear up redness, discharge, and irritation caused by certain bacteria. It only works against bacterial infections and will not help with viral or allergy-related eye problems.
how_it_works: Gatifloxacin is an antibiotic that works by stopping bacteria from being able to copy their DNA, which they need to survive and multiply. Without that ability, the bacteria die off and your infection clears up. Think of it like cutting off the bacteria's ability to reproduce so your body can finish the job of healing.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are mild and happen right in or around your eye. You might notice temporary stinging, burning, or irritation right after putting in the drops. Some people experience eye redness, watery eyes, or blurry vision for a short time after use. These usually go away quickly on their own.
warnings: Do not wear contact lenses while you have an active eye infection or while using this medication. If you are allergic to any fluoroquinolone antibiotic such as ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin, let your doctor know right away. Stop using the drops and call your doctor if you notice a skin rash, severe eye pain, worsening redness, or swelling, as these could be signs of a serious reaction. Never use these drops as an injection and do not swallow them.
typical_dosing: For adults and children 1 year and older, the usual dose is 1 drop in the affected eye every 2 hours while awake on days 1 and 2, then 1 drop up to 4 times a day on days 3 through 7. Always wash your hands before using the drops, and be careful not to let the tip of the bottle touch your eye or any surface to keep it clean. Finish the full course of treatment even if your eye starts feeling better early.
